newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: JG Summit planning IPO for two more units.
newsitem.headline: JG Summit planning IPO for two more units.

text.p: JG Summit Holdings' cement unit will make an initial public offering of shares next year while its petrochemical unit will offer an IPO after three years, JG Summit chief executive officer John Gokongwei Jr said.
Gokongwei was speaking after the listing of an IPO by JG Summit unit Digital Telecommunications which fared poorly in its debut.

Digitel listed 1.27 billion shares representing 20 percent of the company's outstanding capital stock on Wednesday making its debut at 2.80 pesos a share, lower than its 3 pesos offering price. The issue closed at 2.55 pesos.

"The opening was alright. It's hard to tell how the issue fares. These things take two weeks to settle down," Gokongwei said. He did not comment on why the issue may have fallen below its offering price.
The two units which were now slated to go to the IPO market were Apo Cement and JG Summit Petrochemical Corp, he said.
Gokongwei said Apo Cement, which has been in the cement business for 60 years, would begin operations in October of the single biggest cement plant in the country.
The offering date would be between March and June next year depending on market conditions, he said.
JG Summit Petrochemical will be the first in the country to operate a combined polyethylene and a polypropylene plant, two types of petrochemical plants.
Gokongwei said the IPO for the petrochem subsidiary may have to wait for the company's compliance of a three-year track record stipulated by the exchange before the company can go public.
Even though Digitel opened weak, the IPO was oversubscribed, underwriters said.
Digitel's international lead manager Salomon Brothers Hongkong Ltd said that the foreign tranche of the IPO was twice oversubscribed.

"We came in after Deutsche Telekom's $12.5 to $13 billion IPO, and the fact that people showed interest is positive from our point of view," said Hans Brinker M. Sicat, director and head of Philippines investment banking at Salomon Brothers.

PCI Bank president Roberto Panlilio said the domestic tranche of the IPO was also twice oversubscribed. Of the total shares offered, 70 percent was sold internationally while 30 percent was sold to domestic investors.
Besides Digitel, other Gokongwei-backed companies that are publicly-listed include Universal Robina Corp, Robinsons Land Corp, Far East Bank & Trust Co and PCI Bank.

Gokongwei said JG Sumit was likely to post a 3 billion peso recurring net income by the end of the year. Digitel is expected to generate 707.15 million in profits by year-end and 1.79 billion pesos in 1997, he said.
